CONFORMANCE DISCRIMINATOR - a photograph SHOWS the skin resting on the eyelashes but does NOT meet the page-3 submission standards -> Unmet. This is the case the old fused Conforming-Photograph-Shows-X concept could not express at all.

CONFORMANCE DISCRIMINATOR (the other direction) - both lanes conform but NEITHER demonstrates a listed finding (none of the listed) -> Unmet. Conformance alone is not evidence.

PRECEDENCE DISCRIMINATOR - cosmetic purpose on a BOTH-procedure fully documented request -> Unmet. The cosmetic branch is hoisted ABOVE the both/one split; demote it and THIS goes red and nothing else does.
neither procedure requested -> Unmet
PINNED per customer flag 9e2927f3 (resolved, correct as encoded) - the prosthesis indication with its purpose and matching photograph but no listed complaint -> Unmet
MULTI-ANSWER - a packet carrying BOTH a conforming photograph and a conforming visual field -> Met. These are two DIFFERENT coded questions, so they still co-occur after the migration.
OVERLAP ORACLE - photograph shows a listed finding but does NOT conform, while the visual field both conforms and demonstrates -> Met via the VF lane

OVERLAP ORACLE (the separator) - photograph conforms but demonstrates nothing listed, while the visual field demonstrates but does not conform -> Unmet. Neither lane is complete; a flattened conjunction would wrongly pass this.
RECORD ARM - no local attestation at all; a submitted ServiceRequest carrying CPT 15822 is what makes the request true -> Met
BOTH ARMS - a local attestation AND a matching submitted ServiceRequest, same code. The recency arbitration runs and both candidates yield the same answer -> Met

DENY DISCRIMINATOR - a REAL ServiceRequest exists, fully documented, but its code is outside both covered sets -> Unmet. This is what the covered-service value sets are FOR, and it is distinct from requesting nothing at all: absence and non-membership both deny, and only this case proves the second one.
RECORD ARM, both procedures - two submitted ServiceRequests, one per covered set, both individually documented -> Met
